clue.text: Counter-agent seeing point in a new link

indicators.note: in says the point-word sits inside the link-word

parts.note: a tie is something that links or binds
a dot is a small point

explanation.surface: A spy-thriller agent working against the enemy spots a weak point in a new connection.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote counteracts a poison, so it is literally an agent that works against another.

clue.text: Sort of topping month with vermin at home

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August
a rat is a classic piece of vermin
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A month of rats about the house tops everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Au gratin describes a dish finished with a browned crust of breadcrumbs or cheese, a kind of topping.

clue.text: Strip and run escaping from crowd

indicators.note: escaping from says the run letter leaves the crowd-word

parts.note: a throng is a crowd
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone strips off and runs away from the crowd, a streaker's getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow strip of leather or material, as in a sandal strap.

clue.text: Risks losing name for good weapons

indicators.note: losing says the name letter goes from the risks-word
for says the good letter takes its place

parts.note: dangers are risks

explanation.surface: Taking risks costs someone their good name, says a weapon-toting rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Daggers are short stabbing blades, a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Catch on small branch

definitions.meaning: to grasp or understand, informal British
a slender shoot of a tree

explanation.surface: Snagged on a small branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally to twig is to realise or understand; literally it is a slender woody shoot.

clue.text: Relative newcomer's first record cut

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word newcomer's

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
to hew is to cut with blows, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A family newcomer has their first record chopped up.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is a family member, a brother's or sister's son, so a relative.

clue.text: Address English females and finish with one

parts.note: F is female, doubled for the plural
end means finish
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Speak to English women and wrap things up with one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: FF as a plural of the abbreviation F follows the convention of pp for pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi was a Turkish title of respect, a form of address for a gentleman.

clue.text: Extremely happy with a garden designed for growth

indicators.note: extremely takes only the outermost letters of happy
designed says the letters of garden are laid out anew

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled with a garden laid out to encourage plants to flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges GARDEN to DRANGE, and the clue's 'a' ends the answer; 'for' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrangea is a flowering shrub, and growth here means a plant that grows.

clue.text: Grabs wife and relaxes

parts.note: rests means relaxes

explanation.surface: A wife snatches things then puts her feet up.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest something is to seize it with a twisting pull, so grabs.

clue.text: Sticky mess in front of new fridge — oh no!

indicators.note: in front of places the mess-word before the rearranged letters

parts.note: goo is a sticky mess

indicators.note: new says the letters of fridge are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone finds something sticky spilt in front of the new fridge and groans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like a description of the fridge but is the signal to rearrange its letters, giving DGRIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Good grief is an exclamation of dismay, the same cry as oh no.

clue.text: Prepares listener, surrounded by models

indicators.note: surrounded by says the listener-word sits inside the models-word

parts.note: forms are models or patterns
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready, with an eavesdropper hemmed in by fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: To forearm is to arm or ready in advance, as in forewarned is forearmed.

clue.text: Obscure sweet

definitions.meaning: to ... an issue is to blur or obscure it

explanation.surface: An unclear sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means blur or evade an issue; as a noun it is a soft sugary confection.

clue.text: Approach Rome's first person looking for a catch

parts.note: an angle is an approach to a problem or story

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word Rome's

explanation.surface: A newcomer approaches Rome's foremost figure hoping to catch them out.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler fishes, so they spend their time trying to land a fish, a catch.

clue.text: Right answer lies in diplomacy and conduct

indicators.note: lies in says the right-and-answer letters sit inside the diplomacy-word

parts.note: tact is diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: The correct response lies in diplomacy and good conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to carry it out, which is the verb sense of conduct.

clue.text: Aiming for reform outside church state

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters go round the church letters
reform says the letters of aiming are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Campaigners seek reform beyond the church in a political state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges the letters to MIIGAN, and 'outside' wraps them round the church abbreviation; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Michigan is a US state in the Great Lakes region.

clue.text: Looking into getting visa sorted out by heartless Iran

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle of Iran, leaving just its outside letters
sorted out says the letters of getting visa are rearranged

explanation.surface: Officials are examining a visa that was arranged with the help of a callous Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges GETTING VISA to VESTIGATING; 'heartless' leaves IN from Iran, placed first, with 'by' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Investigating is examining or researching a matter, which is looking into it.

clue.text: Filling the place of another priest with evidence of debts

parts.note: a vicar is a parish priest
IOUs are written acknowledgments of debts

explanation.surface: A stand-in priest arrives carrying a stack of unpaid IOUs.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicarious means acting or experienced on behalf of someone else, substituting for them.

clue.text: Officers may see arms laid at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of arms laid are jumbled

explanation.surface: Naval officers might watch weapons being put down on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' doubles as a naval setting, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirals are the most senior officers of a navy.

clue.text: Order Dutch treats, accepting half of mums make the grade

indicators.note: accepting says the rearranged letters take in the other piece
Order is read as a verb, telling us to put the letters of Dutch treats in a new order
half of keeps just the first two of the four letters of mums

explanation.surface: Order Dutch treats that half the mums will approve of and pass muster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads like a purchase but is the anagram signal, giving CUTTHESTARD; 'accepting' then takes in the half of mums.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut the mustard is an idiom for reaching the required standard, succeeding as expected.

clue.text: Teaching and feeling not hot

indicators.note: not says the hot-word is dropped from the feeling-word

parts.note: intuition is a gut feeling
in means hot or fashionable

explanation.surface: Lessons and instinct, minus the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is instruction, especially given privately, so teaching.

clue.text: Constituency must keep network impenetrable with this preparation

indicators.note: must keep says the seat-word holds the network letters inside

parts.note: a seat is a parliamentary constituency
LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: A constituency must keep its computer network secure using this product.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealant is a coating or substance applied to make a surface watertight or airtight.

clue.text: Delicacy of European Community retreat

parts.note: a lair is a hideaway or retreat

explanation.surface: A treat served up in a European Community bolthole.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a fancy cream-filled choux pastry, a dainty treat.

clue.text: Bearing the cost of transport

definitions.meaning: the way a person holds their body, their bearing
the charge made for conveying goods

explanation.surface: Covering the cost of transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage means posture or deportment, and separately the fee for conveying goods, as in carriage paid.

clue.text: Plant some now as a biennial

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gardener plants some now, treating it as a biennial.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is a Japanese brassica whose pungent root is grated as a condiment, so a plant.

clue.text: Anxiety is no good in a way

indicators.note: in says the no-and-good letters sit inside the other letters

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Fretting that things are not good at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a deep feeling of dread or unease, an intense anxiety.

clue.text: Bribe consisting of cake and sugar essentially

parts.note: a bun is a small cake

indicators.note: essentially points to the very centre, the middle letter of sugar

explanation.surface: A sweetener made of cake and sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: Bung is British slang for a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a bung is an illicit payment made to secure a favour.

clue.text: A bit of loin, regularly wanting garlic sauce

indicators.note: regularly says to take every other letter of the phrase, starting from its first

explanation.surface: A piece of pork loin, served as usual, needs a garlicky sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes alternate letters of A BIT OF LOIN; 'wanting' is a link meaning needing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a Provençal mayonnaise strongly flavoured with garlic.

clue.text: Breaking rule again? Such a pain

indicators.note: breaking smashes the letters of rule again and puts them together differently

explanation.surface: Someone flouts the rule once more and is told what a nuisance they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges RULE AGAIN; 'Such a' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is intense pain along the path of a nerve.

clue.text: Feel bitter about attending without power

indicators.note: without says the power letter is taken away

parts.note: to be present is to be attending
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone resents having to attend while stripped of any power.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel aggrieved or indignant about it.

clue.text: Worries stones must contain it

indicators.note: must contain says the stones-word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: agates are semiprecious stones

explanation.surface: Someone frets that the stones must hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate someone is to disturb or trouble them, a verb sense of worries.
